name: desktop_automation
description: Discover and launch installed Windows applications, or open/reveal source-scoped files. Start an application with list_apps(query), then launch_installed_app(app_id) after approval; this catalog launch accepts no path or command arguments and does not require adding system directories as sources. For a source-scoped executable with literal args, use launch_app. Both launch routes survive tool completion. Launchers can hand off to a different process id and name: use computer_observe list_windows to discover the actual app/window, then capture_window before input. Use wait_for_window only with a verified process identity from that inventory. Prefer open_in_nexa for built-in file previews; opening a previewable file externally requires the user's explicit request and external_requested=true. HTTP(S) pages and searches belong to browser_session so the user and Agent share Nexa Browser.

external_requested.description: Set true only when the user explicitly requested opening the file in an external application. Otherwise use open_in_nexa for previewable files.

action.description: list_apps reads Windows App Paths and common system applications; launch_installed_app launches only an exact discovered app_id after approval. Other actions require targets inside active registered sources. launch_app requires an executable file (.exe on Windows).

path.description: Absolute path or source-root relative path for the file or executable. Must resolve inside a registered source directory and the current source scope.

args.description: Literal arguments for launch_app only, passed directly to the executable without shell interpretation. The working directory is the executable's directory.

app_id.description: Opaque appId returned by list_apps in this conversation. Required for launch_installed_app; tokens expire after 5 minutes and each permits one launch attempt. Preview does not consume the token. Never supply a path here.

query.description: Optional application name filter for list_apps, such as Excel, Notepad, or 记事本. This queries installed registrations, not files in source directories.

reason.description: Brief user-facing reason for the desktop file action.
